scripts.//play: The game, on 5174. The editor keeps 5173, and running both at once is the normal way to work on content.
scripts.//shell-build: Windows-only (#103). Builds the client, then packages an NSIS installer. Never part of `npm run land` — see dist-windows.mjs's own header for why.
scripts.build:shell: npm run build --workspace @ed/client && npm run dist:windows --workspace @ed/shell
scripts.//mod-editor-build: Windows-only (#75 B2). Builds the editor, then packages the second NSIS target through the same shell/builder config.
scripts.build:mod-editor: npm run build --workspace @ed/editor && npm run dist:mod-editor --workspace @ed/shell
scripts.//0: test:fast skips the *.slow.test.ts suites — the ones that simulate centuries. What it costs is stated once, in CLAUDE.md, and measured by `npm run cost`: this note said 3s for months while the lane took a hundred.
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck:core && npm run typecheck:editor && npm run typecheck:client
scripts.//1: vue-tsc reads TEMPLATES. Plain tsc cannot, and a template error is always silent — the click lands and nothing happens.
scripts.//2: One local command before you claim the branch works. NOT the gates — native merge-group CI is authoritative.
scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run validate && npm test
scripts.//2a: Local landing preflight: fetch, rebase, install and check the branch, then hand the ready PR to GitHub's native merge queue. The session never pushes main.
scripts.//2b: Did CI actually answer? FOUR states — green, red, pending, and absent. Seven landings on main got no verdict at all and looked exactly like passes.
scripts.//2c: What the agent loop costs, measured the way the game is. Reads the verdict refs, so it needs no API credential a session does not have.
scripts.//2d: Measure what the commands cost and write it into CLAUDE.md. The figures rot when OTHER branches land, so remembering is not a strategy.
scripts.//4: No argument runs every gate — what CI will say, in one command.
scripts.//3: Issue #26's death-spiral gate: the fecundity drag at couplings the shipped constant does not allow. Run it before ever moving that constant.
scripts.//5: Issue #41's measured session: does the marriage decision move carried font? Plays the Match by policy instead of leaving it to the chronicler.
scripts.//6: Issue #41's second half: does the ladder charge the man climbing it? Two played columns, one verb apart.
scripts.//7: Issue #45's acceptance: is bearing a moral or a tax? Three played columns, and the answer is a distribution.
scripts.//11: Issue #99 (Muster stage 4): does the Muster pay, cost, and raise the stakes of the years after it? Two played columns, one verb apart, the same shape as gate:ladder.
scripts.//12: Issue #101: does acreage change, get lost by every route, remain readable across centuries, and leave the treasury constrained?
scripts.//13: Issue #132's Stage 2: once a line thins to one or two, is recovery ever possible, or is broken_line just how it ends?
scripts.//14: Issue #133 Stage 5A-E: one 500-year batch for Ledger, decisions, frame, land/Muster and system reach. Measurement, not a CI threshold.
scripts.//15: Issue #66: Short-Line ending distribution and Ledger-recovery measurement. Use 100 runs to judge the 40% ceiling.
scripts.//17: Issue #274: static Short/Long product inventory — endings, Ledger capacity, ladder vocabulary and campaign-exclusive content.
scripts.//16: Issue #272: paired Short-Line run-two freshness and inherited-Library visibility. Shape overlap plugs into #271's canonical shapeOf.
scripts.//9: Warm the run corpus. Cold, the corpus is SLOWER than replaying; CI caches node_modules/.cache/ed-runs under `npm run corpus -- --key`.
scripts.//10: The mutation probe: break code on purpose, see whether any test notices. A PROBE, run on purpose — never a CI threshold, for the reason docs/TEST-COVERAGE.md gives about coverage.
scripts.//8: Who is working on what, when several agents run at once. The claim is a git ref because every agent authenticates to GitHub as the same user — docs/PARALLEL.md.
